lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: handwashing and surface cleaning

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 3: Kitchen Care and Food Safety
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice handwashing and surface cleaning. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Before doing any food task, the learner is asked to demonstrate the household's full handwashing routine and a proper counter-wipe technique, timing the wash against the 20-second food-safety standard, then compares that wash to a quick rinse with no soap.
materials: learner-local: a sink with soap and water
learner-local: a clean towel or paper towel
learner-local: a clean cloth or paper towel for wiping

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain one way that wiping a counter is similar to washing your hands for food safety, and one way it is different.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Handwashing and wiping technique: The full 20-second soap wash covers palms, backs, fingers, and thumbs, and the counter wipe uses overlapping strokes across the whole surface. | Reasoning about germs and time: The explanation correctly connects soap and full scrub time to removing germs that a brief water-only rinse leaves behind. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner time and compare wiping the same counter with a dry cloth only versus a cloth dampened with soapy water, then explain in writing which method actually lifted more visible crumbs or residue and why.

resources.title: handwashing and surface cleaning worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Before doing any food task, the learner is asked to demonstrate the household's full handwashing routine and a proper counter-wipe technique, timing the wash against the 20-second food-safety standard, then compares that wash to a quick rinse with no soap.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact handwashing and surface cleaning decision or action.
Model move 2: Before washing, predict how long 20 seconds actually feels like.

Model move 3: Wash your hands at the sink using soap, scrubbing the front, back, and between your fingers for a full 20 seconds timed on a clock, then wipe a kitchen counter or table surface using a clean cloth in overlapping strokes.

Model check: Handwashing and wiping technique: The full 20-second soap wash covers palms, backs, fingers, and thumbs, and the counter wipe uses overlapping strokes across the whole surface. | Reasoning about germs and time: The explanation correctly connects soap and full scrub time to removing germs that a brief water-only rinse leaves behind.

5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: handwashing and surface cleaning coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Before doing any food task, the learner is asked to demonstrate the household's full handwashing routine and a proper counter-wipe technique, timing the wash against the 20-second food-safety standard, then compares that wash to a quick rinse with no soap.
Coach direction: Before washing, predict how long 20 seconds actually feels like.
Learner prompt: Guess how many seconds you think you usually spend washing your hands right now, without timing yourself.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: handwashing and surface cleaning complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Wash your hands at the sink using soap, scrubbing the front, back, and between your fingers for a full 20 seconds timed on a clock, then wipe a kitchen counter or table surface using a clean cloth in overlapping strokes.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I used soap and scrubbed my hands, including between my fingers and around my thumbs, not just my palms.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I timed myself for the full 20 seconds instead of stopping early.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I wiped the counter or surface using overlapping strokes so no spot was missed.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

Success checks: Handwashing and wiping technique: The full 20-second soap wash covers palms, backs, fingers, and thumbs, and the counter wipe uses overlapping strokes across the whole surface. | Reasoning about germs and time: The explanation correctly connects soap and full scrub time to removing germs that a brief water-only rinse leaves behind.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: handwashing and surface cleaning supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional handwashing and surface cleaning condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Handwashing and wiping technique: The full 20-second soap wash covers palms, backs, fingers, and thumbs, and the counter wipe uses overlapping strokes across the whole surface. | Reasoning about germs and time: The explanation correctly connects soap and full scrub time to removing germs that a brief water-only rinse leaves behind..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.

safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
